content:
For anyone else confused by "down", as I was - I think I figured out what it means. It's not relative to any particular part of the cable. It's down relative to the printer as a whole.

To help figure it out and visualize it, do this. Hold the string up above the print gantry, flat (in the same plane as the print bed). Have one end above the center of the print bed (like where the print head is in the picture). Have the other end in the back right corner. Use the built-in curve of the string to achieve this, don't force it. When it's in this position, the hooks should be pointing down (toward the print bed).
Remove the cable sleeve completely from the cable and use the textile sleeve tool to insert both the cable and nylon string into the sleeve.

replies.content:
Wait, we have a textile sleeve tool?? This is lifechanging! Which bag is it in?

Edit: despite my enthusiasm above, the nylon was actually much easier to insert into the textile sleeve than other cables have been, and only took a few minutes, no need for removing the cable or any fancy tools.

content: I found it much easier to insert the nylon end into the extruder, then start to run it into the sleeve a few cm.  Install the back cover, then run the nylon into the remaining cable.  It was super hard to get the orientation right - note the "end pointing down" depends on what direction your connector is pointing and its easy to get it wrong.

Use the ball-end of an M2.0 or M2.5 hex driver to guide the sleeve opening. Once the cables and nylon string are inside, run the ball-end of the hex driver along the other side of the cable/nylon string bundle to make sure the sleeve isn't folded over on itself and wraps the correct way. Avoid using anything sharp or you will poke through the sleeve.
